description: Scalp hair morphology: color, texture, pattern, density, hairline shape, and balding patterns. Expands the existing 3-field analysis schema (color/texture/pattern) into a comprehensive trichology-grounded vocabulary. The Andre Walker texture classification (1A-4C) is the de-facto reference for hair texture across populations; the Hamilton-Norwood (male) and Ludwig (female) scales are the canonical balding-pattern references.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with trichology and pigment-genetics literature (MC1R / TYR / OCA polymorphism studies).
dimensions.description: Predominant natural hair color, where determinable. Visibly dyed hair should be flagged via grooming-state metadata.

values.definition: Very dark hair appearing black under normal lighting; high eumelanin.
Distinctly brown but darker than medium-brown.
Standard brown hair.
Light-brown to caramel range.
Dark blonde / dirty blonde.
Standard blonde.
Very light blonde, often near-white. Often dyed in adults.
Red, auburn, or copper. High pheomelanin; correlated with MC1R variants.
Visibly graying hair, mixed pigmented and unpigmented.
Predominantly unpigmented hair.
Multiple distinct natural colors (e.g. natural ombre with sun-lightened tips).
Visible dye job; native color cannot be reliably inferred.

observability.notes: Lighting affects perceived color substantially. Confidence should reflect lighting quality.

dimensions.scale_citation: The Andre Walker hair-typing system (developed in the 1990s for Oprah Winfrey's stylist and subsequently adopted broadly in trichology and beauty-industry literature).
dimensions.description: Andre Walker hair-texture classification covering the spectrum from straight (Type 1) to coily (Type 4), with subdivisions A-C within each numbered type.

values.definition: Stick-straight, very fine; minimal body.
Straight with medium body.
Straight, thick, coarse strands.
Loose S-waves; fine texture.
Defined S-waves; medium texture.
Strong S-waves transitioning to ringlets; coarse.
Loose, soft ringlets; well-defined curl.
Tighter, springy curls; corkscrew shape.
Tight corkscrew curls; densely packed.
Defined small S-pattern coils.
Sharp angular Z-pattern coils.
Tightly packed coils with little visible pattern definition; high shrinkage.
Hair covered by head covering or styling that prevents texture assessment.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with trichology descriptors of follicular density (typical 200-300 follicles/cm² scalp).
dimensions.description: Density of native scalp hair when ungroomed.

values.definition: Visible scalp through hair throughout most of the head.
Some visible scalp; reduced density.
Standard density; minimal visible scalp.
Above-average density.
Pronounced density; voluminous appearance.

observability.notes: Styling affects perceived density; volumizing products and teasing can mask sparse density.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with hair-transplant-surgery descriptors of hairline morphology.

values.definition: Approximately horizontal hairline across the forehead.
Smooth curve hairline; no peaks.
V-shaped point at the midline of the hairline.
Bilateral temporal recession creating an M-shape; common male-pattern feature.
Notable left-right asymmetry.

observability.notes: Hairstyle affects visibility; bangs or fringe can fully obscure hairline.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with hair-transplant-surgery descriptors of hairline-height assessment.
dimensions.description: Vertical position of the anterior hairline.

values.definition: Hairline sits low on the forehead; reduced visible forehead.
Standard hairline position.
Hairline sits high; tall visible forehead.
Recession beyond high-normal; balding-pattern signs visible.

dimensions.scale_citation: Hamilton JB (1951). Patterned loss of hair in man: types and incidence. Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, 53. Norwood OT (1975). Male pattern baldness: classification and incidence. Southern Medical Journal, 68(11).
dimensions.description: Hamilton-Norwood classification of male-pattern hair loss. Applies primarily to subjects with apparent male physiognomy.

values.definition: No hair loss visible.
Earliest stage commonly classified as balding.

values.display_name: Type IV — advanced temporal recession + vertex thinning
Type V — frontal and vertex loss approaching
Type VI — frontal and vertex loss merged

values.definition: Only horseshoe band of hair remaining around sides and back.
Subject not in male-pattern population, or no balding.

dimensions.scale_citation: Ludwig E (1977). Classification of the types of androgenetic alopecia (common baldness) occurring in the female sex. British Journal of Dermatology, 97(3): 247-254.
dimensions.description: Ludwig classification of female-pattern hair loss. Applies primarily to subjects with apparent female physiognomy.

values.display_name: Ludwig I — perceptible thinning of the crown
values.definition: Anterior hairline preserved.
Crown thinning pronounced; anterior hairline preserved.
Crown fully bald; anterior hairline preserved.
Subject not in female-pattern population, or no balding.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in trichology and pigment-aging literature.
dimensions.description: Pattern and extent of visible gray / white hair.

values.definition: No visible gray hairs.
A few isolated gray hairs visible.
Graying concentrated at temples; common early-graying pattern.
Mixed gray and pigmented hair throughout; often ~50/50.
Visible dye job that likely covers gray; native graying state not directly observable.
